outcomes: A user synchronizes a declared environment on the release set its channel points at, with each workload receiving the exact members it owns
The channel an environment follows is read once per run, so every workload of that environment converges on one snapshot
A deploy that shares a session with a publish synchronizes on the set that publish just released
nonGoals: Executing the synchronization: the backend applies the migrations, the configuration, and the image switch, in that order
Ordering or reversing migrations: the CLI carries the members and the migration protocol decides whether a rollback is admissible
Running a progressive rollout: the CLI declares the strategy and the hosting provider performs the traffic split
Deriving an environment from a branch: a branch publishes, an environment follows a channel

requirements.text: A command whose traits declare consumesReleaseSet binds the release set: with --env it resolves the environment's channel or takes --release, selects the workloads the rules name, and hands each of its jobs the set ref and the members of every workload the job covers; with --impacted and a channel it narrows strictly to channel members; beside a publish it waits for the release. A run of no such command warns that --env and --release are undeclared unless a task declares them.
